text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore becomes first Asian country to conclude a liberal open-skies pact with United States, which both sides hope will set the pace for future aviation talks in the Asia-Pacific.
- Singapore Airlines hopes open-skies agreement with U.S. will be "forerunner of many more similar agreements" among and between Singapore and other countries.
- From March 1, people employing foreign maids will have to buy personal accident insurance policy for them before their work permits can be granted or renewed.
- France's Culture Ministry to award grants to talented young cooks and cash-strapped master chefs.
- Man who got away with robery and molest for more than 12 years finally nabbed last year with help of high-tech fingerprint tracking system.
- Singapore emerges as Malaysia's top foreign investor for the first time last year, with total approved investments in manufacturing sector rising sharply to 4.8 billion ringgit.
- Value of non-Singapore dollar trades jumps 29.3 percent to Singapore $9 billion in 1996, reflecting growing importance of foreign currency stocks to total trade on the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
- Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has given his blessings to Singapore Airlines' proposal to set up S$960 million domestic airline with India's Tata group.
- Initial public offer (IPO) fever infects foreign-currency stocks, with mould base maker Lung Kee Metal Holdings making impressive debut on Thursday.

- In largest foreign investment in Taiwan's newly liberalised property market, Government of Singapore Investment Corp takes 10 percent stake in what local claim will be world's most expensive shopping mall.
- With the stags in full play in hot IPO market, several broking analysts expect a premium of at least 50 percent for Second Chance Enterprises when it debuts.
- Datacraft Asia posts 75 percent jump in interim net profit to US$4.64 million.
- Metro Holdings converts most of its 58,000 square feet of space in Lucky Plaza from retail to office use.
